purpose: Cinacalcet is used to lower high levels of parathyroid hormone (PTH) in people with chronic kidney disease who are on dialysis. It is also used to treat a condition called primary hyperparathyroidism, where the parathyroid glands are overactive. In addition, it can help manage high calcium levels caused by parathyroid cancer.
how_it_works: Your parathyroid glands control the amount of calcium in your blood. Cinacalcet works by making these glands more sensitive to the calcium already in your blood, which tells them to slow down and produce less PTH. Less PTH means your body releases less calcium from your bones, helping to keep your calcium and PTH levels in a healthier range.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, especially when you first start taking it. You may also experience low calcium levels, which can cause muscle cramps, tingling or numbness in your hands or feet, or feelings of dizziness. Some people also experience loss of appetite or headaches.
warnings: This medication can cause dangerously low calcium levels (hypocalcemia), which can lead to seizures or serious heart rhythm problems, so your doctor will regularly check your blood calcium. Do not take cinacalcet if your calcium levels are already too low. Tell your doctor if you have seizures, heart problems, or liver disease. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medication. Always swallow the tablet whole with food — do not crush or chew it.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults on dialysis is 30 mg taken by mouth once a day with food or shortly after a meal. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose every 2 to 4 weeks (up to a maximum of 180 mg per day) until your PTH and calcium levels reach the right range. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as doses vary depending on your condition.
